# Agriculture — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Crops, Seeds & Plants: typically around 2,000, most listings 1,000-4,500 (3 listings)
- Farming Tools & Machinery: typically around 45,000, most listings 10,000-300,000 (3 listings)
- Other Agriculture: typically around 1,000, most listings 60-23,000 (10 listings)

All rows are thin (n ≤ 10) — treat these as rough anchors and lean on general judgment.
For high-value machinery (power tillers, pumps, tractors, mills), a price far below the
plausible market range is a scam signal -> hold; cheap seeds, saplings, and produce at
low prices are normal here.

## What good listings look like
- "Bela Belt coffee beans 1kg" — NPR 2,150
- "table bamboo plant with pot" — NPR 750
- "ZIG ZAG PLANT" — NPR 5,000
- "Rudrasha garfting biruwa" (grafted rudraksha sapling) — NPR 50,000
- "Coffee for Barista training" — NPR 1,650

A good listing names the specific crop/plant/tool, plus quantity or unit (per kg, per
sapling, per piece) and condition for machinery. Nepali-language titles are common and fine.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Frequent miscategorized posts land here: samples include a photo frame, Pringles snacks,
  and a flute. Obvious non-agriculture items (decor, packaged snacks, instruments) -> hold
  for recategorization.
- Rudraksha is common in this category and a known scam space in Nepal: listings claiming
  rare mukhi counts (ek mukhi etc.) or divine/certified rarity at prices far above the
  ordinary bead/sapling market -> hold.
- Business-front ads (a farm advertising itself with a token price rather than selling a
  specific item, e.g. "कृषि फर्म" at NPR 65) -> hold unless a concrete product and real
  price are stated.
